name: deleting a handle no engine could have minted is a 400
description: The pair to delete-blob.json, and the reason it has to be a fixture rather than a unit test: the two together are the whole delete contract, and a runner that got one right and the other wrong would look correct. A well-formed handle pointing at nothing is a 200 (deletion is idempotent); a handle the engine could not have minted is a 400, because with 'already gone' reported as success it is the only remaining failure that is not a backend fault, and answering 500 would tell an operator the service is broken when the caller sent nonsense. Note the asymmetry with read-blob-bad-handle.json, which answers 404 for this same handle: read cannot act on the difference between malformed and gone, so it collapses both. A 500 from delete therefore means one thing only — the backend failed and the bytes may still be there.
